[[Category:Glasgow Name Study]]

== Biography ==
'''John Glasgow''' was born about 1740 in Ayrshire, Scotland. An indexed Scottish birth or baptism record gives the date '''28 March 1740''' at Irvine and identifies him as a son of [[Glasgow-1058|George Glasgow]] and [[Martin-103040|Margaret Martin]].<ref name="John1740">"Scotland Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XTVL-9BN : accessed 28 July 2026), John Glasgow, 28 March 1740; citing FHL microfilm 1,041,383.</ref>

John is probably the '''John Glasgow who married or partnered with Margaret Mill''' and later lived at West Calder, Midlothian. Their son Peter Glasgow was baptised there on 10 October 1762.<ref name="Peter1762">"Scotland, Births and Baptisms, 1564–1950," database, FamilySearch (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4T-5P2 : accessed 28 July 2026), Peter Glasgow, baptised 10 October 1762 at West Calder, Midlothian, son of John Glasgow and Margaret Mill; duplicate parent entry (https://familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:VQ4T-5PL : accessed 28 July 2026), John Glasgow in entry for Peter Glasgow.</ref>

The identification of the Irvine-born John with Margaret Mill's husband is a strong working hypothesis, but has not yet been confirmed by a marriage record or another document explicitly connecting Irvine and West Calder.

John's corresponding FamilySearch profile is:

* [https://www.familysearch.org/en/tree/person/9Q1F-9BL John Glasgow, FamilySearch ID 9Q1F-9BL]

The supplied extracts for Andrew, Margaret, Agnes, Issobel and Janet identify John as their father but do not display their mother's name. Their dates and placement with the same FamilySearch family make Margaret Mill the probable mother, but the original entries should be checked.

An 1800 marriage index associates an unidentified woman surnamed Glasgow with Alexander Hunter. She may have been one of John's daughters, but the extract does not preserve enough information to identify her securely.<ref name="Hunter1800">"Scotland, Marriages, 1561–1910," database, FamilySearch (https://www.familysearch.org/ark:/61903/1:1:XYSW-FB4 : accessed 28 July 2026), Glasgow in entry for Alexander Hunter, 1800.</ref>

== Research Notes ==
=== Individual father review, 22 October 2026 ===

The existing father [[Glasgow-1058]] is assessed at 84% (probable). John’s 1740 Irvine transcript names George Glasgow and Margt Martin. The existing George/Margaret Martain couple has a 1728 Kilwinning marriage and 1729 child, giving a distinctive compatible parental sequence before Irvine.

Complete father-profile placement84%; the 1687 George child’s identification with this adult remains an inference. Original uninspected.

Next useful test: Compare the Kilwinning and Irvine couple’s residences, occupations and witnesses.

Source basis already held: [https://www.findmypast.co.uk/transcript?id=SCOT%2FOPR%2FBAP%2F3574953&tab=this Findmypast, Scotland, Parish Births & Baptisms 1564-1929: John Glasgow, 30 Apr 1740, record SCOT/OPR/BAP/3574953]. No new original inspected; no new father attached.



=== Identification as Margaret Mill's husband ===

The John Glasgow baptised or recorded at Irvine in 1740 is the leading candidate for the John Glasgow who later had children with Margaret Mill at West Calder.

Evidence supporting the identification includes:

* John would have been about 22 when Peter was baptised in 1762.
* Margaret Mill was reportedly born about 1740, making the couple similar in age.
* No separate wife or family is presently attached to the Irvine John.
* The names '''Andrew''', '''Margaret''' and '''Agnes''' occur among both his probable siblings and his proposed children.
* The wider family appears to have moved between Ayrshire, Edinburgh, western Midlothian and Linlithgowshire.
* Another member of the connected family, Thomas Glasgow born in 1725, reportedly married Janet Isobel Mill, suggesting repeated association between the Glasgow and Mill families.

The principal weakness is that no marriage, testament, sasine, kirk-session entry or other record has yet been found stating that John of Irvine became the husband of Margaret Mill at West Calder.

The repeated use of '''Andrew''' in the next generation is of particular interest. John and Margaret Mill reportedly named a son Andrew in 1764, and their son Peter later named another son Andrew in 1790.

Naming repetition is supportive but does not prove identity.

=== Son Peter and the Bathgate family ===

John and Margaret's son Peter, baptised in 1762, is probably the '''Peter or Patrick Glasgow''' who later had children with Elizabeth Dick at Bathgate.

Peter and Elizabeth's family included:

Peter and Patrick were often used interchangeably in Scottish records. The continuous sequence of children, the same wife and the same locality make it highly likely that Peter and Patrick were the same person.

The eldest son, '''John Glasgow''', reportedly born on 7 June 1783 and baptised on 6 July 1783, is probably the John Glasgow who later married Jean Bryce and worked as a shop porter in Canongate, Edinburgh.

The recurrence of Andrew, Margaret, Agnes, John, Elizabeth and Peter is consistent with a single extended family. Most of the names were common, however, and the pattern cannot substitute for direct documentary evidence.

=== Wider family and migration pattern ===

The connected descendant tree places members of this broader Glasgow family in:

* Edinburgh during the seventeenth century;
* Kilwinning, Irvine and Stevenston in Ayrshire;
* Livingston, Mid Calder and West Calder;
* Bathgate in Linlithgowshire;
* Canongate, Edinburgh, during the early nineteenth century.

This makes the movement from Irvine to West Calder, then Bathgate and Canongate, geographically plausible.

The connected CC7 descendant report places John baptised in 1740 among the children of George Glasgow and Margaret Martin and within a wider line descending from John Glasgow, born in Edinburgh in 1661.<ref name="CC7">WikiTree CC7 descendant report generated from the connected descendants of [[Glasgow-1097|Archibald Glasgow]], supplied 28 July 2026. The report reflects current WikiTree relationships and is a research aid rather than independent proof.</ref>

=== Possible earlier ancestry ===

The connected WikiTree structure proposes:

The descent from Archibald Glasgow is not established. The early connected tree contains a serious chronological conflict: Archibald's reported death predates the reported birth of one supposed son. Every generation before John Glasgow and Agnes Spark should therefore be independently verified.

The earlier marriage of Archibald Glasgow and Isobell Neulands may indicate a longstanding association between the Glasgow and Newlands families. It does not prove that the later Newlands connections in the descendants of John born in 1783 came through Isobell.

=== Alternative candidates ===

Another John Glasgow was baptised on 2 July 1721 at Kilwinning, a son of Hugh Glasgow and Janet Kilpatrick.

He could also have been the husband of Margaret Mill, but he would have been about 41 when Peter was baptised in 1762 and substantially older than Margaret. The 1740 Irvine John is therefore the better chronological match.

John Glasgow, baptised in 1750 at Mid Calder, can effectively be excluded as Peter's father under the current dates because he would have been only about twelve in 1762.

An otherwise unrecorded collateral John remains possible.

=== Research priorities ===

* Find the marriage or proclamation of John Glasgow and Margaret Mill.
* Examine the original West Calder baptism of Peter Glasgow dated 10 October 1762.
* Examine the original baptisms of Andrew, Margaret, Agnes, Issobel and Janet to confirm their mother.
* Trace the Irvine John through kirk-session records, tax rolls, land records, testaments and burials.
* Search Irvine, Kilwinning, Stevenston, West Calder and neighbouring parishes for evidence of the family's movement.
* Identify the Glasgow woman who married Alexander Hunter in 1800.
* Compare witnesses in the West Calder baptisms with George Glasgow, Margaret Martin and their known children.
* Treat the identification of John born in 1740 as Margaret Mill's husband as probable rather than proved until a direct bridging record is found.
* Treat the proposed descent from [[Glasgow-1097|Archibald Glasgow]] as unproved until each intervening generation is documented.
